JUDGMENT Heard Sri. Ravindra R. Mane, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri. Anoop G.Deshpande learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
2. The present appeal is filed by the insurer challenging the liability fastened on the insurer wherein the claim petition filed by the claimants on account of death of Rudrappa allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.5,13,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization is awarded in favour of the claimants.

3. Sri. Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the goods vehicle in question as such the liability could not have been fastened on the insurer.

He would also submit that since the vehicle involved in the accident is a goods carrying vehicle, unless the person traveling in the goods vehicle along with the goods, the insurer cannot be made liable to pay the compensation and no evidence is placed to show that the deceased was traveling in the goods vehicle along with the goods.

4. Sri. Anoop G.Deshpande, learned counsel appearing for the claimants would submit that it is admitted in the cross-examination that the deceased was traveling with vegetables and based on the admission in the cross-examination, the Tribunal has rightly held that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

5. Sri. Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel would refer to Section 2(13) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 wherein the word 'goods' is defined.

The expression reads as under:
"'goods' includes livestock, and anything (other than equipment ordinarily used with the vehicle) carried by a vehicle except living persons, but does not include luggage or personal effects carried in a motor car or in a trailer attached to a motor car or the personal luggage of passengers traveling in the vehicle."
6.
By referring to the said definition, it is contended that the personal luggage carried in a motor vehicle cannot included in the term of the goods.
7. This Court has perused the records and evidence placed.
8. It is to be noticed that the claimants are not able to establish that the deceased was traveling in the vehicle along with the goods.
However, what it is required to be noticed is, there is a policy issued by the insurer.

Under these circumstance, this Court is of the view that the insurer has to satisfy the award as far as the claimants are concerned and thereafter liberty is reserved to the insurer to recover the compensation amount from the owner of the vehicle.
To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Trial Court are modified.
9. It is to be noticed that the claimants have not filed any appeal or cross objection seeking enhancement.
However, it is required to be taken note of the fact that the deceased was a coolie and coming from the poor background.

Though the claimants have not filed cross objection seeking enhancement under Order XLI Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure, to do complete justice, this Court is of the view that the compensation payable to the claimants be re-assessed by taking into consideration the parameters set out by the Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
10.

The notional income should be taken at Rs.5,000/- per month and 10% is to be added towards the future prospects.
The multiplier would be 13 and 1/3rd of the income should be deducted towards personal expenses.

Accordingly, the loss of dependency would be Rs.5,72,000/- [i.e. Rs.5,000 + 10% future prospects X 12 months X 13 multiplier X 2/3].
11.

In terms of law laid down in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.
PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, each claimant is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium. Rs.30,000/- is awarded under conventional head and the same is awarded as shown in the chart below.

 Less: Amount awarded by the Tribunal 5,13,000/-
 Enhanced Compensation 2,49,000/-
13.
Since the claimants have not filed appeal, this Court is not inclined to grant interest on the enhanced compensation.
Claimants are entitled to interest on the compensation determined by the Tribunal.
Appellant - insurer shall deposit the compensation before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

14. Since the accident has taken place in the year 2009, this Court is of the view that the entire compensation amount has to be released in favour of the claimants in the ratio determined by the Tribunal.
15. The judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified as indicated above.
Accordingly, appeal stands disposed of.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
